hints: Focus on writing the full balanced equation for the combustion of one mole of S8, not just one sulfur atom.
Count how many O=O bonds must be broken and how many S=O bonds are made when 8 molecules of SO2 form.
Use the Hess idea that enthalpy change equals energy in to break all reactants to atoms minus energy out when product bonds form, then solve for one S=O.
walkthrough:
**Write the balanced combustion equation**

Think of what actually burns. One mole of S8 makes 8 moles of SO2.

$$\text{S}_8(\text{s}) + 8\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 8\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H = -2376 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Break everything to gaseous atoms, then rebuild**

To use bond enthalpies, first make atoms. Breaking S8(s) to 8 S(g) costs +2232 kJ. Breaking 8 O2 to 16 O atoms costs energy too.

$$\text{energy in} = 2232 + 8(496) = 2232 + 3968 = 6200 \text{ kJ}$$

**Form the product bonds and solve**

Each SO2 is O=S=O, so it has 2 S=O bonds. For 8 SO2 that is 16 S=O bonds in total. Let S=O = x.

$$\Delta H = \text{energy in} - \text{energy out}$$
$$-2376 = 6200 - 16x$$
$$16x = 6200 + 2376 = 8576$$
$$x = 536 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

options.A: Reverses the Hess sign by using energy out minus energy in. It calculates 16x - 6200 = -2376, giving 16x = 3824 and x = 239. Remember, breaking bonds is endothermic (+), making bonds is exothermic (-), so Delta H = broken - formed.
options.B: Subtracts the O=O breaking energy instead of adding it, as if O2 is formed not broken. It does -2376 = 2232 - 496 - 16x, giving 16x = 4112 and x = 257. All reactant bonds broken, including all 8 O=O, must be added as energy in.
options.C: Uses only 1 O2 molecule instead of 8. It does -2376 = 2232 + 496 - 16x, giving 16x = 5104 and x = 319. The balanced equation needs 8 O2 to make 8 SO2, so you need 8 x 496 kJ to get O atoms.
options.D: Correctly accounts for stoichiometry: 8 O2 broken and 16 S=O bonds formed. -2376 = 2232 + 8(496) - 16x gives 16x = 8576, so x = 536 kJ mol-1.
